title: GH Pages CI/CD
summary: Ships a React + Vite app as a static site on GitHub Pages: build to dist/, set Vite's base path to the repo name, use HashRouter in production (GitHub Pages can't route /about), and deploy with the gh-pages package. Then GitHub Actions runs Cypress on every push and pull request (CI) and deploys automatically (CD). Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Deploy a React app to GitHub Pages and set up a GitHub Actions workflow that runs tests before deploying.

steps.title: Read both lessons
steps.detail: Read 'GitHub Pages for Static Sites' and 'GitHub Actions CI/CD', especially 'BrowserRouter Is Not Suitable for GitHub Pages'.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain why a refresh on /about gives a 404 on GitHub Pages.

steps.title: Build Myflix and look at dist/
steps.detail: A production build turns your JSX into plain static files. Run this in the Myflix folder and open the preview URL.
steps.code:
cd ~/Desktop/codeplatoon/assignments/week-02/netflix
npm run build
npm run preview
steps.doneWhen: A dist/ folder appears with index.html and an assets/ folder, and the preview works.

steps.title: Read the deploy settings you'll need
steps.detail: The lesson adds "predeploy": "npm run build" and "deploy": "gh-pages -d dist" to package.json and sets base: "/YOUR_REPOSITORY_NAME" in vite.config.js. For cruzjay188/netflix that would be "/netflix". Myflix also needs its Supabase settings at build time; keep .env out of git and ask in #eagle_questions how they want env vars handled in Actions.
steps.doneWhen: You can name the three changes Myflix would need to deploy.

steps.title: Walk through the Cypress workflow
steps.detail: Read the lesson's .github/workflows/cypress.yml and label each part: on (when it runs), jobs (what machine), steps (checkout, install, run tests).
steps.doneWhen: You can say in plain English what triggers the workflow and what it does.

concepts.meaning: Plain HTML, CSS and JS files served as-is, with no server code.
The folder npm run build creates with the files you actually deploy.
A router that keeps the page path after a #, so static hosts never see it.
Automatically running tests on every push or pull request.
Automatically publishing the app when tests pass.
